findings.body: The input's documented behaviour changed, but the `examples/` mirror of the docs-sync set is missing: `examples/open-source-safe.yml` documents this exact input (comment block at lines 11–30, usage at line 79) and `examples/README.md` describes it, yet neither was touched. Per this repo's sync rule (README + CHANGELOG + setup reference + at least one `examples/` file), add a one-line note to the example — e.g. that private/internal repos additionally get the collaborator-permission fallback while public repos stay association-only.

If the payload lacks `repository.visibility` (older GHES payloads, relayed event shapes), this returns `"unknown"` and the whole permission fallback becomes inert — the override requires private/internal and failures fail-closed on unknown — so the fix this PR ships silently doesn't apply. Every `pull_request` payload also carries the older `repository.private` boolean; a one-line fallback keeps the feature working there:

```suggestion
    visibility: str = str(repository.get("visibility", "") or "").lower()
    if not visibility and repository.get("private") is True:
        visibility = "private"
    return visibility or "unknown"
```

This is the same call as `test_permission_api_failure_private_fail_open` (line 2354) — the resolver cannot distinguish "lookup attempted and failed" from "lookup never attempted" (both arrive as `permission_lookup_failed=True`), so it adds no coverage. The actually uncovered branch is the `main()` wiring (missing `user.login` or malformed `AIPRR_REPO` → `permission_lookup_failed=True`); a small `unittest.mock.patch` case (pattern already used in `tests/test_iar_*.py`) would cover it for real.

The known permission-levels vocabulary is inlined here while its write-tier subset lives in the module constant `COLLABORATOR_PERMISSION_WRITE_TIER` added in this same PR. Promote the full set beside it (e.g. `COLLABORATOR_PERMISSION_KNOWN_LEVELS`) so both follow the constants-at-top convention.

## Verdict

Solid, well-tested feature — the permission-aware gate is implemented defensively (fail-closed on unknown visibility, 404 → non-collaborator, username URL-quoted) and all 12 new tests pass locally along with `py_compile`. One warning needs a small fix before merge: the new API call fires on public repos where its result can never change the outcome, breaking the documented "denied gate costs zero API calls" contract.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning | `scripts/reviewer.py:6399` | Permission lookup runs on public/unknown-visibility repos where the result is discarded — contradicts README's "zero API calls" and SECURITY.md's "on private/internal" text |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `action.yml:71` | `examples/open-source-safe.yml` documents this exact input but wasn't updated (docs-sync set is 3 of 4) |
| 3 | ℹ️ info | `scripts/reviewer.py:5317` | No `repository.private` fallback when `visibility` is absent — the fix silently becomes inert on such payloads |
| 4 | ℹ️ info | `tests/test_reviewer.py:2411` | `test_lookup_skipped_private_fail_open_via_lookup_failed` duplicates the test at line 2354; the real gap is `main()` wiring |
| 5 | ℹ️ info | `scripts/reviewer.py:632` | Known permission-levels tuple inlined; its write-tier sibling is already a module constant |

Good.
